## reasoning ##
1. The workload is TPC-C with 16 concurrent clients on only 4 vCPUs, so the configuration should favor short indexed OLTP operations and avoid parallel-query and JIT startup overhead.
2. The observed 90.15% buffer-hit rate and high read-I/O level indicate that the previous shared_buffers value of 16384 blocks was undersized; increasing it to 1310719 blocks provides approximately 10 GiB of PostgreSQL cache without consuming an excessive fraction of 30.82 GiB RAM.
3. effective_cache_size is raised to 3014657 blocks, approximately 23 GiB, so the planner accounts for PostgreSQL and operating-system cache and is more willing to select indexed access paths.
4. enable_indexscan remains enabled because TPC-C queries depend heavily on primary-key and secondary-index lookups, while the measured ExecInsertIndexTuples and B-tree insertion activity is inherent to the workload.
5. cpu_tuple_cost and cpu_operator_cost are reduced moderately to represent memory-resident tuple and predicate processing more accurately and support efficient indexed plans without making extreme planner-cost changes.
6. Parallel execution is discouraged because short OLTP statements generally cannot amortize worker setup, tuple transfer, and synchronization costs on a 4-vCPU server.
7. max_parallel_workers_per_gather is limited to 1, force_parallel_mode remains off, parallel_setup_cost and parallel_tuple_cost are increased, and both minimum parallel scan sizes are raised to prevent marginal parallel plans while preserving parallelism for unusually large scans.
8. JIT is disabled because compilation, expression generation, tuple-deforming, inlining, and optimization overhead normally outweigh execution savings for short TPC-C statements; the individual JIT features are disabled consistently.
9. Nondefault, nonboundary JIT cost thresholds are retained as inert safeguards so that enabling JIT later would still require relatively expensive statements before compilation is attempted.
10. debug_print_plan, debug_pretty_print, log_planner_stats, log_executor_stats, and log_disconnections are disabled to eliminate formatting, statistics collection, and logging work from the benchmark path.
11. max_wal_size is increased to 6143 MB to reduce checkpoint frequency and associated buffer-lock and write-pressure effects under the write-intensive TPC-C workload.
12. fsync remains enabled to preserve crash-safe WAL durability, while synchronous_commit is disabled to remove foreground WAL-flush waits identified through XactLogCommitRecord and XLogFlush; this improves throughput at the cost of potentially losing the most recent acknowledged transactions after an operating-system crash.
13. commit_delay and commit_siblings are assigned nonboundary values, although commit-delay behavior has little practical effect while synchronous_commit is disabled.
14. cursor_tuple_fraction is reduced because TPC-C statements and cursors generally consume small result sets, favoring plans with low startup cost.
15. idle_in_transaction_session_timeout is set to 60001 ms to clean up abandoned transactions and prevent long-lived locks without interfering with normal benchmark transactions.
16. These changes are intended to bridge the measured 1568.817234 TPS result toward 1584.505406 TPS, but the exact result must be validated with repeated, equivalently warmed benchmark runs because storage latency and checkpoint timing can affect measured throughput.
